stemMarkdown: A man sells two articles at the same price. On one he gains 15% and on the other he loses 15%. What is his overall percentage profit or loss on the whole transaction? (Enter a negative value for a loss, rounded to 2 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Let each SP be 10000. Then CP of the first is $\dfrac{10000}{1 + 15/100} = 8695.65$ and CP of the second is $\dfrac{10000}{1 - 15/100} = 11764.71$. Total CP $= 20460.36$ against a total SP of 20000, a net **loss** of $2.25\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Whenever two items sell at the same price with equal gain and loss percentages, the result is always a loss of $\dfrac{x^2}{100} = \dfrac{225}{100} = 2.25\%$ — never a break-even.
